Design document: LLM-based user profile system from Edge browser behavioral signals

Goal
- Produce a five-layer, derived-user-profile system that summarizes browser behavioral signals with LLMs and serves them synchronously (<5ms P99) to a real-time AI assistant, while never storing raw behavioral events on the server (only derived profile layers), being GDPR/CCPA-compliant, and giving users view/delete controls.

Summary of approach
- Client sanitizes & aggregates behavioral signals and sends minimal, non-PII payloads to an ephemeral server-side pipeline.
- Server-side pipeline batches/summarizes signals (embedding + clustering + LLM) into the five-layer profile (L1..L5).
- Profiles are stored as compact JSON per user in a fast KV cache (primary read path, Redis-like) with async replication to durable document store for audit/backups.
- Reads are synchronous (assistant reads the profile at request time). Writes are async/eventual.
- Profiles exposed via user APIs (view, export, delete). PII detection runs at all LLM and storage boundary points.

SECTION 1 — Full profile schema (JSON/pseudo-JSON)
Notes:
- All fields are derived; zero raw events/URLs/search strings stored. Evidence fields contain aggregated/sanitized paraphrases, counts, dates, not raw payloads.
- All timestamps are ISO-8601 strings; confidences are floats in [0.0,1.0].
- Each layer stored as its own JSON object under user profile key. Each layer has meta: version, last_updated, update_method.

L1 — Identity (monthly)
- Purpose: stable attributes that change rarely.
- Size target: compact (few hundred bytes).
Schema (pseudo-JSON):
{
  "layer": "L1",
  "version": 17,                                // integer
  "last_updated": "2026-04-10T12:00:00Z",
  "identity": {
    "occupation": {                             // nullable
      "value": "Software Engineer",
      "confidence": 0.92,
      "inferred_from": ["long_term_domain_freq", "bookmarks_category"],
      "last_inferred": "2026-04-10T12:00:00Z"
    },
    "expertise_domains": [                      // array
      {
        "name": "Web Development",
        "subdomains": ["TypeScript","React"],
        "proficiency": "intermediate",          // {novice|intermediate|advanced}
        "confidence": 0.85,
        "evidence_count": 48,
        "last_activity": "2026-04-24"
      }
    ],
    "communication_style": {
      "tone": "concise",                        // {formal|casual|concise|verbose}
      "formality": "casual",
      "verbosity": "short",                     // {short|medium|long}
      "use_emojis": false,
      "confidence": 0.70
    },
    "languages": [{"code":"en-US","confidence":0.99}],
    "time_zone": "America/Los_Angeles"
  },
  "meta": {
    "update_method": "monthly-llm-v1",
    "notes": "Derived only — no raw events stored"
  }
}
Example values: shown above.

Relation to other layers:
- L1 provides priors for L2 (preferences) and L3 (interpretation of interests). L1 is slow-moving and used as a prior when LLM must disambiguate short-term signals.

L2 — Preferences (weekly)
- Purpose: how the assistant should format responses & avoid topics.
Schema:
{
  "layer": "L2",
  "version": 9,
  "last_updated": "2026-04-25T03:00:00Z",
  "preferences": {
    "preferred_content_length": "short",        // {short|medium|long}
    "preferred_format": ["bullet_list","code_snippets"], // ordered
    "formality": "casual",
    "topics_to_avoid": [{"topic":"cryptocurrency","confidence":0.9}],
    "preferred_source_style": "concise_summaries_with_links",
    "default_action_preferences": {
      "open_links_in_new_tab": true,
      "show_sources": true
    },
    "privacy_preferences": {
      "store_personal_notes": false
    },
    "confidence": 0.82
  },
  "meta": {"update_method":"weekly-llm-v1"}
}
Example values: as above.

Relation:
- L2 modifies how assistant uses L1/L3 for response shaping. L2 is the personalization policy for the assistant.

L3 — Interests (daily)
- Purpose: active interest clusters that drive content personalization.
Schema:
{
  "layer": "L3",
  "version": 32,
  "last_updated": "2026-04-26T02:30:12Z",
  "interests": [
    {
      "id": "int_15a9",                         // stable cluster id (hash)
      "topic_label": "Edge caching & CDN strategies",
      "canonical_keywords": ["edge caching","CDN invalidation","cache-control"],
      "confidence": 0.92,
      "trend": "increasing",                    // {increasing|stable|decreasing}
      "last_seen": "2026-04-25T16:20:00Z",
      "evidence_count": 21,
      "source_breakdown": {"page_visits":12,"searches":6,"bookmarks":1,"copy_events":2},
      "summary": "Active reading and searches about caching/CDN strategies; likely tied to a work project."
    }
  ]
}
Example values: shown above.

Relation:
- L3 drives L4 (world context) and L5 triggers. Assistant uses L3 as the topical prior for generation.

L4 — World Context (daily)
- Purpose: short-term focus, active projects, recent searches/news topics.
Schema:
{
  "layer": "L4",
  "version": 5,
  "last_updated": "2026-04-26T06:00:00Z",
  "context_snapshot": {
    "active_projects": [
      {
        "project_id":"proj_a1b2",
        "title":"Design caching layer for CDN strategy (paraphrase)",
        "status":"in-progress",
        "related_interest_ids":["int_15a9"],
        "last_activity":"2026-04-26T05:44:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "recent_search_topics":[{"topic":"cache-control headers", "last_searched":"2026-04-26T04:10:00Z","count":3}],
    "recent_news_topics":[{"topic":"edge computing pricing changes","last_seen":"2026-04-25","count":2}],
    "session_summary":"Preparing a spec about CDN invalidation strategies"
  },
  "meta":{"history_days_kept":7}
}
Example values: shown above.

Relation:
- L4 is ephemeral, used to adapt responses to the user’s immediate context (e.g., incorporate current project details).

L5 — Interest Cards (event-triggered, transient)
- Purpose: transient cards surfaced to user or assistant when a pattern suggests a short-lived intent.
- TTL default: 48 hours (extend on user action).
Card schema (cards array):
{
  "layer":"L5",
  "version": 12,
  "last_updated":"2026-04-26T10:12:00Z",
  "cards":[
    {
      "card_id":"card_20260426_1",
      "type":"purchase_intent",                // e.g., purchase_intent, deep_reading, travel_planning
      "created_at":"2026-04-26T10:12:00Z",
      "expires_at":"2026-04-28T10:12:00Z",
      "title":"Considering noise-cancelling headphones",
      "content_summary":"Multiple product-category visits and comparisons detected (sanitized counts).",
      "recommended_actions":["price_tracking","summarize_reviews","save_for_later"],
      "evidence":{"distinct_products_viewed":4,"visits":7,"searches":3},
      "confidence":0.88,
      "dismissed":false,
      "source_aggregates":{"domains_count":3,"bookmarks":1}
    }
  ]
}
Examples: above.

Relation:
- L5 cards are surfaced immediatly to the assistant or UI. They expire automatically and are stored with short TTL.

SECTION 2 — Generation pipeline (how each layer is produced)

Global principles
- Raw event handling: the browser sanitizes and aggregates events client-side (remove PII, paraphrase text, replace named entities with types when necessary) before sending them into the server pipeline. Server-side ephemeral queue holds events for a bounded short window (e.g., <24 hours in-memory or encrypted buffer) for processing; no raw events are persisted to durable storage.
- Processing steps used across layers:
  - Feature extraction (counts, scroll-depth stats, time-of-day histograms)
  - Embedding + clustering of sanitized textual items (titles / paraphrases / search-topics)
  - LLM summarization to produce human-readable labels, summaries, confidences
  - Validation & PII-scan on outputs
- Output writing: background worker writes updated layer to profile store (Redis) and publishes an update event (no raw events in payload).

Layer-by-layer details

L1 — Identity
- Input:
  - 90-day aggregates: domain frequency (top-N domains), bookmarks categories, persistent login to career sites (paraphrased), long-term search-topic paraphrases, explicit profile fields (if user consents).
  - Signals: page_visits (long-term counts), bookmarks, saves, domain categories
- LLM summarization prompt (template):
  - System: "Infer stable identity attributes from these aggregated, sanitized signals. Output ONLY valid JSON matching the schema. Do NOT invent personal data or include PII."
  - Input: sanitized list of top domain categories with counts, paraphrased long-term search topics (no raw queries), explicit fields.
  - Task: infer occupation, high-confidence expertise domains, preferred communication style.
- Trigger: monthly scheduled job or when a stable-change signal is observed (e.g., repeated LinkedIn/company profile visits, new declared occupation).
- Merge strategy: weighted merge with exponential decay:
  - If old value exists, new_value = normalize( alpha * new_inference + (1-alpha) * old_value ), alpha tuned by evidence_strength (alpha ∈ [0.2,0.6]); update confidence accordingly.
  - For categorical fields, prefer new if evidence_strength > threshold (e.g., 0.8).
  - Overwrite only when new confidence > old_confidence + delta (delta=0.15).
- Write semantics: overwrite the identity object with merged result (store previous version in audit log).

L2 — Preferences
- Input:
  - 7-day aggregates: read length histograms (scroll depth, dwell time), explicit saves/likes, reaction types, content format interactions (copy/highlight frequency).
- LLM summarization prompt (template):
  - System: "From aggregated usage patterns, infer presentation & content preferences. Output JSON with fields: preferred_content_length, format, topics_to_avoid etc."
- Trigger: weekly schedule OR immediate when explicit user preferences change (e.g., UI change).
- Merge strategy:
  - Mostly overwrite semantics with recency weighting: if new signals are consistent (>=70% of last-week signals agree), replace; else combine via majority & confidence weighting.
  - Conflicts handled by tie-breaking: prefer explicit user signals (bookmarks, explicit setting) > inferred.
- Writes: update L2 object (version increment).

L3 — Interests (detailed, includes full prompt example below)
- Input:
  - 24-hour aggregates (or sliding 24h): sanitized paraphrases of titles/search-topics, top domains, counts of interactions (visits, search-clicks, highlights, copies), time-of-day.
  - Preprocessing: client/sanitizer creates paraphrased short text items (no raw urls, no full query text if PII). Server computes embeddings and clusters.
- Pipeline steps (recommended):
  1. Compute embeddings (on sanitized paraphrases).
  2. Run clustering (HDBSCAN / agglomerative) to form candidate clusters.
  3. For each cluster, summarize top keywords & counts.
  4. Send cluster summaries to LLM to create human-readable labels, short summaries and confidence estimates.
- LLM summarization prompt: see "Full prompt example for L3" below.
- Trigger: scheduled daily OR adaptive: process immediately if user generated >N signals in short window (e.g., >20 relevant interactions in 2 hours).
- Merge strategy:
  - Per-cluster merge: if new cluster matches an existing cluster id (cosine similarity of cluster centroid > 0.75 or keyword overlap Jaccard > 0.6), then merge:
    - merged_confidence = (old_confidence*old_evidence + new_confidence*new_evidence) / (old_evidence + new_evidence)
    - evidence_count = old_evidence + new_evidence
    - last_seen = max(old_last_seen, new_last_seen)
  - If no match — append new cluster.
  - Prune clusters with confidence < 0.2 or evidence_count < min_threshold (e.g., 2) after merge.
- Writes: replace/merge interest list in L3 using optimistic concurrency (version/ETag).

Full prompt example for generating/updating L3 (complete)
System instruction:
"You are a privacy-aware summarization assistant. Input is sanitized aggregated behavioral signals (no raw URLs, no raw queries). Produce exactly one JSON object that conforms to the provided schema. Do not invent names, addresses, or other PII. Use only the aggregated evidence provided. Confidence must be a float between 0.0 and 1.0. Output only JSON, no explanation text."

User input (sanitized):
{
  "user_hash":"u_abc123",
  "period":"2026-04-25T00:00:00Z/2026-04-25T23:59:59Z",
  "top_domains":[{"domain_category":"tech_research","visits":6},{"domain_category":"developer_qa","visits":4},{"domain_category":"developer_blogs","visits":3}],
  "paraphrased_search_topics":[{"topic":"transformer model fine-tuning","count":3},{"topic":"edge caching strategies","count":5}],
  "content_interactions":[{"type":"highlight","count":8},{"type":"copy","count":2}],
  "bookmarks_categories":[{"category":"tech_articles","count":2}],
  "time_of_day":"work_hours",
  "session_count":10
}

Task:
"Using only the sanitized aggregates above, produce interests[] with fields:
  - id: stable cluster id (short)
  - topic_label: short human-friendly label
  - canonical_keywords: list of 3-8 tokens/phrases
  - confidence: 0.0-1.0
  - trend: {increasing|stable|decreasing}
  - last_seen: ISO date
  - evidence_count: integer
  - source_breakdown: {page_visits, searches, bookmarks, copy_events}
  - summary: 1-2 sentence paraphrase of why the cluster exists (no raw URLs/queries)
Maximum clusters: 10. Prefer clusters that have evidence_count >= 2."

Expected output (example)
{
  "layer":"L3",
  "last_updated":"2026-04-26T02:30:12Z",
  "interests":[
    {
      "id":"int_edgecache_01",
      "topic_label":"Edge caching & CDN strategies",
      "canonical_keywords":["edge caching","CDN invalidation","cache-control"],
      "confidence":0.92,
      "trend":"increasing",
      "last_seen":"2026-04-25T16:20:00Z",
      "evidence_count":21,
      "source_breakdown":{"page_visits":12,"searches":6,"bookmarks":1,"copy_events":2},
      "summary":"User actively reads and searches about caching and CDN strategies, likely for a work-related project."
    },
    {...}
  ]
}

L4 — World Context
- Input:
  - Current session context: open tabs (categories only), recent searches (sanitized topics), recently edited docs (if consented), active tasks inferred from session (paraphrase).
- LLM summarization prompt:
  - "Summarize user's current focus: list active projects, recent search topics, and session summary. Output JSON snapshot."
- Trigger: daily snapshot OR on session start / when session has >M related actions.
- Merge strategy: replace daily snapshot; keep recent history (last 7 snapshots) for cross-day context.

L5 — Interest Cards (event-triggered)
- Input:
  - Immediate patterns in sanitized signals produced by client or server (counts, sequences).
- Card trigger patterns (3 concrete patterns):
  1. Purchase intent card
     - Trigger: within 48h user visited product-category pages on >= 3 distinct product pages (domain_category = "ecommerce_product") and distinct_products_viewed >= 3 and combined visits >= 5 OR user added same-category items to bookmarks/wishlist multiple times.
     - Create type: "purchase_intent"
  2. Deep-dive / summarize card
     - Trigger: user scroll_depth >= 90% + highlights >= 5 + copy events >= 1 on a long article within a 24h window.
     - Create type: "deep_reading" offering a summary, Q&A, or citation extraction.
  3. Travel planning / itinerary
     - Trigger: repeated searches and page visits for the same city/place across multiple domains within 48h (>=3 interactions from travel_category) or bookmarking multiple travel guides for same destination.
     - Create type: "travel_planning"
- Card schema (fields, as shown in L5 section above):
  - card_id, type, created_at, expires_at, title (paraphrase), content_summary (sanitized), recommended_actions (enum), evidence (counts), confidence, dismissed, source_aggregates.
- Expiry & eviction logic:
  - Default TTL: 48 hours from created_at.
  - Extend TTL by +48 hours on user interaction with the card (e.g., user requests summary or saves).
  - Evict immediately if dismissed by user or contradictory signals (e.g., user explicitly marks "not interested").
  - Global cap: max 20 active cards per user; eviction policy LRU or lowest-confidence-first if cap exceeded.
- Trigger & write:
  - Event-driven: immediate card creation writes to L5 layer in profile store with expires_at field. Also push notification to assistant UI if allowed.

SECTION 3 — Storage and serving architecture

Constraints recap:
- Read P99 < 5ms
- 10M users at scale
- ~2KB/profile average -> ~20GB raw data
- No raw behavioral data stored
- Reads synchronous; writes async/eventual

Design summary
- Primary read store: distributed in-memory KV (Redis Cluster / Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise or equivalent).
  - Reason: in-memory gives sub-ms reads, scalable sharding, built-in TTL and eviction, replication.
  - Key format: profile:{user_hash}
  - Value: compact serialized JSON with L1..L5 layers or a subset (layer mask) to minimize payloads.
- Durable backup & audit store: document DB (Azure Cosmos DB / DynamoDB) or object storage for periodic snapshots of derived profiles and audit logs (only derived data). This store used for compliance export & restore.
- Event ingestion: ephemeral stream (Kafka / in-memory queueing) with very short retention (<24h) and strict access control. No raw events persisted to disk beyond this short window.
- LLM workers: autoscaling compute cluster that reads ephemeral events, performs summarization, writes to Redis and durable store asynchronously.

Sizing & configuration (approx.)
- Data: 10M * 2KB = 20GB; add metadata/overhead -> provision Redis memory ~80–128GB to allow replication and headroom.
- Cluster: Redis Cluster with 6+ shards, replication factor 2 (or Redis Enterprise with clustering), AOF/RDB snapshot for persistence.
- P99 latency: Redis reads from memory are typically <1ms–3ms; add regional proximity to Edge, and local in-process caches for micro-optimizations.
- Durable store: CosmosDB with partition key user_hash; writes from summarizer are async (throttled).

Caching strategy
- Primary cache = Redis (authoritative for live reads).
- L0 local in-process short-lived cache per assistant worker:
  - TTL: 30s–1min for repeated requests during same conversation to reduce Redis calls.
  - Invalidation: publish/subscribe channel from Redis; background worker publishes profile update messages (profile-update:{user_hash}) so instances can invalidate local cache.
- Layer-level fetch: assistant requests can include layer mask to fetch only needed layers (e.g., L2+L3 only) to minimize network/serialization overhead and privacy exposure.

Read (sync) path
1. Assistant service receives a user request.
2. Calls ProfileService:GetProfile(user_hash, layer_mask).
3. ProfileService:
   - Check local in-process LRU cache (very short TTL).
   - If miss -> query Redis key profile:{user_hash} (or profile:{user_hash}:layers if per-layer sharding).
   - Validate version/ETag; return JSON to assistant synchronously (<5ms target).
4. Assistant uses the profile data to condition the generation. Only required fields for the current task are forwarded into assistant LLM prompt to minimize exposure.

Write (async) path
1. Summarization worker completes aggregation and LLM summarization for some layer.
2. Worker writes merged layer JSON to Redis with version & ETag using CAS to avoid race conditions.
3. Worker publishes update on Redis pub/sub or messaging bus (profile-updates) for local cache invalidation.
4. Worker asynchronously writes full derived profile snapshot to durable store for compliance/audit export.
5. For reliability: writes to durable store are retried/backed off; Redis write is primary for real-time reads.

Consistency & concurrency
- Use version numbers & optimistic CAS writes to prevent older summarizations from overwriting newer data.
- Each update includes meta: {version:int, last_updated:ISO}. Workers read current version before merge and increment.

Security & privacy at rest and in transit
- TLS for all in-transit communications.
- Redis encryption at rest if supported; durable store encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys.
- Access control: only summarization workers and profile service can mutate profile keys.

SECTION 4 — LLM summarization pipeline (detailed)

Goals
- Balance cost and quality.
- Minimize LLM call sizes & token counts by pre-clustering and summarizing.
- Ensure robust output parsing, PII filtering, and retries.

Event batching and flow
- Client-side:
  - Browser collects events, sanitizes & reduces (paraphrases titles, redacts PII, converts URLs -> domain/category).
  - Batches are sent periodically or on thresholds to server’s ingestion endpoint.
- Server-side ephemeral queue:
  - Short retention (configurable, default 24 hours). No long-term storage.
  - Worker pulls batched sanitized events for user u, performs preprocessing (embedding, clustering) and summarization.
- Batching rules:
  - L1: cumulative 90-day aggregates built from weekly incremental updates (server maintains rolling derived stats only).
  - L2: week-window batch (7 days or sliding).
  - L3: 24-hour window; adaptive-trigger if high activity.
  - L4: per-session window OR daily snapshot.
  - L5: immediate event triggers.

Model choices (recommended)
- Two-tier strategy:
  - Frequent, low-latency layers (L3, L4, L5): use a fast/cheaper model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini / Llama-2-13B quantized or an internal distilled model). Tradeoff: lower cost, slightly lower nuance.
  - High-impact/low-frequency layer (L1 monthly; L2 weekly): use higher-quality model (e.g., GPT-4.1 / Claude-2.1 or highest-quality internal model) to capture nuance.
- Use embeddings model for clustering (text-embedding-3-small or internal) — cheaper than repeated LLM summarization.

Prompt structure (principles)
- Provide explicit JSON schema and "output MUST be valid JSON" instruction.
- Provide sanitized aggregated inputs as structured fields (counts/keywords).
- Require confidence calibration and short justifications (evidence_count) but disallow raw events.
- Include strict PII filter instruction: if any output would contain PII, replace with canonical placeholder, and flag for review.

Full prompt example for L3 (see section above). Use the same style for L1/L2/L4 prompts but adjusted for their schema and timescales.

Output parsing & validation
- Steps:
  1. Parse LLM output as JSON.
  2. Validate against a strict JSON Schema (types, required fields, value ranges).
  3. PII-scan output using NER + regexes (emails, phone numbers, SSNs). Reject outputs that contain PII tokens.
  4. Sanity checks: confidence ∈ [0,1], evidence_count ∈ integer>=0, number of clusters <= max.
  5. If validation fails:
     - Attempt auto-repair: re-prompt LLM with "Output must be JSON only" and the failing output included, instruct to fix.
     - If second attempt fails, fall back to deterministic heuristics (e.g., use top domain categories as interest label) and emit an anomaly log.
- Record results in audit logs (derived only) with LLM model id, prompt hash, output validation status, no raw inputs.

Failure handling
- LLM call transient failure:
  - Retry up to N=2 attempts with exponential backoff.
  - If still failing, keep previous layer state unchanged, emit metric and alert.
  - For high-importance layers (L1), queue for offline reprocessing with human-in-the-loop if required.
- LLM returns garbage/invalid:
  - Try re-prompt auto-repair once.
  - If still invalid, fallback to deterministic algorithmic summarization (clustering labeler based on top keywords).
- Monitoring:
  - Track per-user and per-layer failure rates, invalid JSON rate, PII rejections.
  - Alert if failure rate exceeds threshold.

Operational controls
- Rate-limit LLM calls with priority to real-time needs (L5 immediate cards, L3 adaptive) and backlog low-priority jobs.
- Keep model, prompt and schema versions in metadata to support audits and rollbacks.

SECTION 5 — Evaluation framework

Principles: measure utility, accuracy, stability, and privacy compliance.

Offline evaluation
- Datasets:
  - Consent-labeled dataset: recruit users (opt-in) who provide ground-truth labels for interests/preferences via surveys; capture derived signals in the client for offline mapping.
  - Synthetic/annotated dataset: human raters label clusters generated from sanitized signals.
- Metrics:
  - Interest detection: precision@K, recall, F1 @ cluster level vs ground truth.
  - Calibration: expected calibration error (do confidence scores match empirical accuracy).
  - Stability: JS divergence / cosine distance between consecutive daily profiles (should not fluctuate excessively).
  - Compression/Error trade-off: how often does the profile lose important content vs. size targets.
- Evaluation pipelines:
  - Re-run summarizer on held-out data and compute above metrics.
  - Human-in-the-loop spot-checks for L1 (monthly) outputs.

Online evaluation (production metrics)
- Engagement & quality:
  - Assistant satisfaction: thumbs-up rate, direct ratings.
  - Clarification rate: number of assistant follow-up questions per conversation (expected reduction).
  - Time-to-task-completion: average time or steps to complete a task with and without profile personalization.
  - CTR on recommended actions (cards).
  - Retention & session length (longer-term).
- Safety & privacy:
  - Number of PII-detection incidents (LLM output flagged).
  - Profile deletion/export requests per 100k users (monitor spikes).
  - Percentage of profile reads that were served to the assistant (usage coverage).
- System reliability:
  - LLM failure rate, validation failure rate.
  - Redis read latency P99 (<5ms target).

A/B testing
- Core experiment: Does the profile improve assistant quality?
  - Control: Assistant uses only session context (no persistent profile).
  - Treatment: Assistant uses L2+L3 (preferences & interests) to personalize responses.
  - Randomization: user-level split (stratify by geography/timezone/usage level).
  - Primary metric: user satisfaction (thumbs-up rate) per request.
  - Secondary metrics: time-to-task, clarification rate, retention.
  - Duration: run until statistical significance (precomputed sample size for power 0.8).
  - Safety checks: monitor PII/Error metrics, stop experiment if negative safety signals.
- Incremental experiments:
  - Feature gating: test L1-derived persona changes vs no-change.
  - L5 cards surfacing vs no cards.

Privacy compliance check (runtime & deployments)
- Automated PII checks:
  - All outputs pass PII detection before storing; any PII triggers redaction and audit.
- Human review policy:
  - Only aggregated, derived data goes to human reviewers for edge case debugging; raw events are never available.
- Deletion & export:
  - API endpoints:
    - GET /profile?user_hash=...&layers=... -> returns derived profile (user-visible).
    - DELETE /profile?user_hash=... -> remove Redis key, remove durable snapshots associated with this user (or mark for deletion), publish deletion event, invalidate caches.
    - GET /profile/export?user_hash=... -> export derived profile JSON (user-facing).
  - On delete: immediate deletion from Redis; asynchronous deletion from durable store/backups per retention policy with audit record of deletion.
- Consent & audit:
  - Store user consent records (which derived attributes allowed) separately (minimal metadata only).
  - Detailed audit logs for changes to profile (derived only, no raw signals) preserved for compliance, with delete markers and retention policy.

SECTION 6 — Operational & design tradeoffs / open questions

Tradeoffs called out
1. Model quality vs cost:
   - Higher-quality LLM for L1 yields better identity inference but is expensive. Strategy: use high-quality LLM only monthly for L1; use cheaper models for frequent updates (L3/L5).
2. Client vs server processing:
   - Sending sanitized paraphrases from client reduces server raw-data risk but increases client complexity. Alternative: server does more sanitization but must ensure no raw event storage.
3. Staleness vs freshness:
   - More frequent L3 updates increase freshness but cost and noise; we use adaptive triggering to balance.
4. Storing embeddings:
   - Storing full embeddings for fast re-clustering speeds reprocessing but consumes storage and could be considered more sensitive. Option: compute embeddings ephemeral and don't persist.
5. Reproducibility & audit:
   - We store derived profile snapshots for audits; but frequent snapshots increase storage. Strategy: keep periodic snapshots + deltas.

Open questions (to be decided with product / legal)
- How much paraphrased contextual detail is allowed in the profile vs. considered too close to raw data? (Needs legal sign-off.)
- Is client-side embedding generation allowed/feasible to further reduce server-side raw data flow?
- How aggressive should the system be in surfacing L5 cards to users (UX tradeoff)?
